AcceptReach.description:
Accept one to 50 of an actor's paths for one reason and a period of days (#355, step 4).
Accepting one already accepted renews it.
AcceptReach.title: AcceptReach

AcceptedPath.description:
One path whose acceptance stands, to withdraw: any kind an acceptance is recorded for,
since `accept-reach` also accepts an observed path (#355, step 4).
AcceptedPath.title: AcceptedPath

AcknowledgeFinding.description: An optional note; `{}` acknowledges with none. The store trims and screens it.
AcknowledgeFinding.title: AcknowledgeFinding

AcknowledgeFindings.description: One to 50 distinct canonical finding identifiers and one optional note for them all.
AcknowledgeFindings.title: AcknowledgeFindings

ActionChangeView.description:
An action the policy newly maps (wider when one of its own allow rules names it) or no
longer maps.
ActionChangeView.title: ActionChangeView

ActionRules.description: One action's rules, in the order the compiler writes them.
ActionRules.title: ActionRules

ActivationNote.description:
The latest activation of a bundle in a Space the reader can see: when, by whom, and
the reason recorded with it. `reason` is null for an activation that gave none (the CLI
without `--reason`, quickstart, the samples). The reason is a person's text and the
console renders it as text.
ActivationNote.title: ActivationNote

AgentView.description:
A principal on a record: its id, label, kind and the workspace's counting number, so
the console names it "Agent 3" or "User 3" when it has no label (#678).
AgentView.title: AgentView

ApprovalDelivery.description:
What happened to the approval's announcements, and when the last one arrived.

The counts are over `approval.pending` rows only. `lapsed` is a message closed unsent
because the approval lapsed first; `closed`, one the approval's decision beat; and
`withdrawn`, one whose request stopped being valid before anyone decided it. `margin_seconds`
is the deadline less the last delivery, in whole seconds, negative when the message arrived
after it. `late` is true when a message lapsed unsent or arrived within
`LATE_DELIVERY_SECONDS` of the deadline, or after it.
ApprovalDelivery.title: ApprovalDelivery

ApprovalItem.description: One row of the queue; the detail carries the same item first.
ApprovalItem.title: ApprovalItem

ApprovalSpace.description: The space that owns this approval, which the console opens the link in.
ApprovalSpace.title: ApprovalSpace

ApprovalWindow.description:
How long a held request for one action can wait at most (#678).

An upper bound: the smallest validity over the kinds of fact the action's contract resolves,
through the bundle's own context settings, capped by the deadline. A request waits less,
because its time starts when its facts were recorded. `known` is false where a custom policy
may hold the action; `limited_by` is `unknown`, with no figure, where a contract is unknown.
ApprovalWindow.title: ApprovalWindow

ApprovalWindowSpace.description: One Space's held actions; none, with no bundle, where no policy is active.
ApprovalWindowSpace.title: ApprovalWindowSpace

BindOption.description: What the other side of a binding can be: an agent for a principal, or the reverse.
BindOption.title: BindOption

BoardCounters.description:
The figures across the top, counted by the server so no viewer's clock is involved.

`limited` and `refused` are known for the window and not for the day: a limit refusal is
read from the codes its denial recorded, by the rule that tells the denied agent `limit`,
and a request refused before a decision leaves no execution row at all, and both of those
are bounded reads over the window rather than the day's tally. `null` says "not counted for
this period", which is a different statement from zero and the only honest one here.
BoardCounters.title: BoardCounters

BoardLane.description: One row of the board. `index` is server assigned and is the only id the client draws.
BoardLane.title: BoardLane

BoardObservation.description: One thing monitoring saw and the checkpoint did not decide.
BoardObservation.title: BoardObservation

BoardShot.description: One request, at the phase its state puts it in and the age its event times give it.
BoardShot.title: BoardShot

BoardView.description: The whole board, as one value, for one moment the server fixed.
BoardView.title: BoardView

BudgetChangeView.description: One budget that differs, each side's ceiling in words.
BudgetChangeView.title: BudgetChangeView

BundlePreviewView.description:
What the candidate would have decided over the tenant's own recent frozen history.

`available` is false when the history could not be exported or verified; the page says so
rather than showing zeroes, exactly as the Jinja page's note does.
BundlePreviewView.title: BundlePreviewView

Change.description: When a setting last changed and who changed it.
Change.title: Change

CompiledPolicy.description: The compiled bundle, read-only. It is what the kernel executes; the rules are its source.
CompiledPolicy.title: CompiledPolicy

ConnectTines.description:
A Tines connection: its name, the tenant's address, an optional team and the API key,
which is sealed for the collector and never stored, shown or logged.
ConnectTines.title: ConnectTines

ConnectionChange.description: No fields: the address names the connection and the change.
ConnectionChange.title: ConnectionChange

ConnectionSchedule.description:
A connection's intervals in seconds; left out or null, the kind's default. Entra
collects every 3,600 to 86,400 seconds; Tines reads its audit records every 300 to 3,600
and its inventory daily, which is not adjustable.
ConnectionSchedule.title: ConnectionSchedule

CreateSource.description:
One Tines story to report: a name for it, the story's ID, how long its token lives and
how often it sends a heartbeat.
CreateSource.title: CreateSource

DirectoryInvitation.description: A pending invitation: when it stops working, and nothing about the code itself.
DirectoryInvitation.title: DirectoryInvitation

DirectoryLink.description:
The account a person signs in with at the tenant's own directory.

`subject` is the identifier; the two display values are hints the directory reported and
are shown as text, never used to find anybody. `via` says who bound it.
DirectoryLink.title: DirectoryLink

EntraConnectStart.description:
Microsoft's sign-in address for this attempt. Its `state` is a secret for ten minutes:
the console navigates to it and keeps it nowhere.
EntraConnectStart.title: EntraConnectStart

ExpiringKey.description: A used agent key that expires within seven days and that no live key replaces.
ExpiringKey.title: ExpiringKey

ExpiringKeys.description: At most five agents, each by its soonest key, and how many more there are.
ExpiringKeys.title: ExpiringKeys

ExternalCase.description: Unverified caller-supplied navigation, never trusted incident context.
ExternalCase.title: ExternalCase

Governed.description:
The credential `Govern this agent` issued, with what to do next; the secret is above
the recipes and never inside them.
Governed.title: Governed

IssuedCode.description:
A one-time set-password code, with the page to open and nothing else.

It comes back in the mutation response that minted it, which is `Cache-Control: no-store`
like every console response; the client shows it once in the same dialog a credential is
shown in. The code is not part of the address, so nothing carrying it is ever a link.
IssuedCode.title: IssuedCode

IssuedCredential.description:
The one-time secret with its identifiers.

It comes back in the one mutation response that created it, which every console response
already sends as `Cache-Control: no-store`; the client shows it once in a dialog and holds
it nowhere else. The audit chain records the identifiers only.
IssuedCredential.title: IssuedCredential

scope.default: Synthetic example policy; not your workspace policy. No provider is called.
scope.title: Scope

LimitMeter.description:
One limit rule with the use admission would count against it.

`used` is `None` where the rule's scope has no single tenant-wide figure; `counted` says
which, in the words the page prints, so a blank meter is explained rather than empty.
LimitMeter.title: LimitMeter

MintedSource.description:
A source's token, shown once: the console holds it in one dialog and nowhere else. The
intake address is the deployment's configured origin, never the request's.
MintedSource.title: MintedSource

MonitorAcceptance.description: One acceptance of a path, or its withdrawal, as `monitor_reach_acceptances` keeps it.
MonitorAcceptance.title: MonitorAcceptance

MonitorAcknowledgements.description: One answer per requested finding, in request order, as the server decided it.
MonitorAcknowledgements.title: MonitorAcknowledgements

MonitorConnectAttempt.description:
How the session's own latest Microsoft Entra consent attempt ended, if it ended within
the last ten minutes: what the page says on the return from Microsoft. Never a code, and
never another person's attempt.
MonitorConnectAttempt.title: MonitorConnectAttempt

MonitorConnectOptions.description:
Which providers this deployment connects from the console. `unconfigured` means the
console shows who connects one instead of a form that cannot work. Where Microsoft Entra is
available, the platform app's name as a directory administrator sees it and its client id,
which the console names when it says how to withdraw consent. `sources` says whether the
console mints reporting sources, which it does exactly where Tines connects, and
`intake_url` is where a reporting story sends its events, from the configured origin.
`placement` is where something made now lands, or null where the session sees several
Spaces and has chosen none.
MonitorConnectOptions.title: MonitorConnectOptions

MonitorDestination.description:
One findings destination (#31), as the private configuration names it: its id, kind,
host, rules and Spaces, never its URL, address or secret. `rules` and `spaces` are null
where it takes every one; a configured Space the reader cannot read is counted in
`other_spaces`, never named. For a reader of every Space, `other_spaces` is 0 and a
configured id that is no Space of this workspace is counted in `unknown_spaces`; for any
other reader such an id is counted in `other_spaces`, so a hidden Space and a mistaken id
look the same.
MonitorDestination.title: MonitorDestination

MonitorDriver.description:
One piece of evidence of who drives an actor (#355), kept apart from what it can reach.

`declared`: the directory names the driver, as the AI publisher catalog's entry for the
principal's application or an agent identity's blueprint. `network`: its successful sign-ins
came from a range the reviewed egress catalog attributes to a platform, or from an address an
administrator recorded as the Space's Tines tenant's egress; it names a platform, never a
workflow. `joined`: that Tines evidence plus every story in the Tines tenant that uses a
credential allowed to call Microsoft Graph or Microsoft sign-in (`story_ids`, "at least" where
`stories_capped`); it never names one story as the one that acted. A catalog row names its
source and the day it was read; a Tines row counts the tenant's credentials with no host
restriction, which are never joined. `label` is a catalog's name or, for a Tines tenant, the
connection's own name, and renders as text.
MonitorDriver.title: MonitorDriver

MonitorDriverGaps.description:
What no network evidence can name: platforms that publish no stable egress, whose actors
cannot be attributed by network, and those whose published feed has not been read into the
catalog yet.
MonitorDriverGaps.title: MonitorDriverGaps

MonitorDriverSummary.description:
An actor's strongest current driver row the reader may see (#355, step 4): its level, what
kind of platform it names, and the platform's name, which renders as text.
MonitorDriverSummary.title: MonitorDriverSummary

MonitorFindingAgent.description:
The directory agent a finding of an agent rule is about. The sponsors are counted, not
sent.
MonitorFindingAgent.title: MonitorFindingAgent

MonitorFindings.description:
The findings in one state, newest first and at most 200, with both totals counted in
SQL beyond the page, and the active detection profile.
MonitorFindings.title: MonitorFindings

MonitorPlacement.description:
Where a connection or a reporting source made now lands: the session's Space by id and
name, whether it is archived, and whether this administrator administers it. An administrator
narrowed to Spaces sees Spaces they only review, and adds nothing there. The id lets the
console tell a placement read before the session moved to another Space, which it reads
again.
MonitorPlacement.title: MonitorPlacement

MonitorSyntheticDirectory.description:
The workspace's synthetic directory, which holds for every Space (#355, step 4), read for
the workspace rather than for the Space the session looks at. `present`: one is active, so
no Space connects Microsoft Entra. `addable`: none is active and no Space ever connected
Microsoft Entra, said only to a reader of every Space and false to anyone else.
MonitorSyntheticDirectory.title: MonitorSyntheticDirectory

NotificationDelivery.description:
How fast this workspace's announcements arrived over the last week (#678).

Counts and durations only, over `approval.pending` rows, workspace-wide as the deadline is.
Durations are whole seconds rounded up; the percentiles are null below five deliveries.
NotificationDelivery.title: NotificationDelivery

PasskeyOptions.description:
The WebAuthn request options, as `py_webauthn` serialises them, for this session's
single-use challenge.
PasskeyOptions.title: PasskeyOptions

PasswordChange.description:
A person changing their own password, presenting the current one.

Both bounds are the store's, restated here so a body outside them is refused as
`INVALID_BODY` naming the field rather than reaching the hash at all.
PasswordChange.title: PasswordChange

PolicyComparison.description:
How a policy differs from the one active in the reader's Space, as the rules read.

Never a decision: the preview shows what would actually have decided differently. A change
that adds a connector account, declares an external executor or turns off observe-only is
a change here too, so such a draft never reads as no change. `why_not` says why nothing
was compared: no single Space chosen, no active policy there, this is the active policy,
or one side is written in Cedar rather than as rules.
PolicyComparison.title: PolicyComparison

Proposed.description:
One rule the compiler accepted against the draft, as the add-a-rule form takes it.

`sentence` is how it reads, `lines` are its conditions in the words the editor parses,
and `rule` is the form's own shape. Nothing here has been written: the person submits it.
Proposed.title: Proposed

Provider.description: One registered provider. No secret and no ciphertext: neither is read for this view.
Provider.title: Provider

QualifierOptions.description:
What a single-action budget of this bundle may be counted for, besides each agent and
the whole tenant, as `_qualifiers` reads it inside the tenant's fence.
QualifierOptions.title: QualifierOptions

ReachPath.description:
One path of an actor's, as its reach rows name it: one Accept offers, a live grant, role
or inherited path.
ReachPath.title: ReachPath

RecordEgress.description:
The addresses a Tines tenant's HTTP requests leave from, as Tines shows them at
`/info`: at most eight single public addresses; an empty list clears them. Recording them
re-reads thirty days of the Space's directory sign-ins once.
RecordEgress.title: RecordEgress

ReplaceConnectionKey.description: A new API key for a sealed Tines connection.
ReplaceConnectionKey.title: ReplaceConnectionKey

ReportView.description:
What ExecBound recorded for requests made in the window, in the reader's scope.

`refused_before_decision` is null where it cannot be scoped to the reader: such a refusal
names no target or space. `monitoring` is an administrator's alone.
ReportView.title: ReportView

RevokeOtherSessions.description: The confirmation carries nothing but the session's token, as the form does.
RevokeOtherSessions.title: RevokeOtherSessions

RotateSource.description:
How long the replacement token lives, and how many minutes the previous one keeps
reporting (none, 10, 30 or 60, and never past its own expiry).
RotateSource.title: RotateSource

RuleChangeView.description:
One rule that differs, with how each side reads; `before` or `after` is null when the
rule is added or removed.
RuleChangeView.title: RuleChangeView

RuleName.description:
One rule of the active bundle's ruleset about this action: its effect and its name.

The two stay apart so the page can print the effect as a word and link the name to the
rules page, rather than build a link out of a sentence. Empty for a path the rules do not
reach, and for every row of a bundle written as a document.
RuleName.title: RuleName

RuleRow.description:
How one rule reads. Labelled on the page as the rules' wording, never as the decision,
which is the kernel's and is made from the compiled policy below it.
RuleRow.title: RuleRow

RulesFileSummary.description:
Whether this policy's rules download as a rules file, and what the file leaves out
because it names this workspace's own records: the budgets counted for a named group,
account or Space, and the context settings.
RulesFileSummary.title: RulesFileSummary

RulesFileView.description: A policy's rules as the file `ruleset-compile` reads, with what it leaves out.
RulesFileView.title: RulesFileView

RulesView.description: A draft's rules, and everything the form needs to add one the compiler will accept.
RulesView.title: RulesView

SampleChange.description: Every change takes an empty object; the session says whose workspace it is.
SampleChange.title: SampleChange

ServiceLinksView.description:
The deployment's support address and public pages, each null where it names none, and
a link with no address is not shown (`execbound.service_links`).
ServiceLinksView.title: ServiceLinksView

SessionSpace.description: The space this session is looking at; `null` is "All spaces".
SessionSpace.title: SessionSpace

SettingsDirectory.description:
`provider` is null when nothing is offered: no provider is enabled, or this deployment
holds no key ring, so the link route would answer 404. `link` is null when this person has
no active link. An approver's link is removed by an administrator on the approver's page; an
administrator's link is not removed from the console.
SettingsDirectory.title: SettingsDirectory

SettingsDirectoryLink.description:
The acting person's own account at the tenant's directory.

`subject` is the identifier; the two display values are hints the directory reported, its
text and not a person's, shown as text and never used to find anybody. `via` says who
bound it: the person themselves, an administrator, or an invitation they redeemed.
SettingsDirectoryLink.title: SettingsDirectoryLink

SettingsDirectoryProvider.description:
The tenant's enabled provider, the one a person links their own account through.

Its id, its name and its state only: the issuer, the client id and the secret are an
administrator's (`/tenant/sign-in`) and are not read for this view.
SettingsDirectoryProvider.title: SettingsDirectoryProvider

SettingsSecurity.description: The person's own second factor (#678): counts and flags only, never a secret.
SettingsSecurity.title: SettingsSecurity

SignIn.description:
How this person signs in, beside the credentials they hold.

`has_password` says whether one is set and never anything about it; `pending_until` is
when an unredeemed set-password code stops working. Neither the hash nor the code's
digest is read for this view, so neither can reach a response by accident. The name is
`has_password` rather than `password` because the shared secret guard refuses a key
called `password` in any rendered output, and a boolean should not be the exception.
SignIn.title: SignIn

SignInView.description:
What the tenant settings page shows about signing in with the customer's directory.

`configured` is false when the deployment holds no key ring, in which case there is nowhere
to keep a client secret and the page says so rather than offering a form that cannot work.
SignInView.title: SignInView

SignalRecordView.description:
One frozen record a signal fact rested on, for an administrator.

Every field the plan froze and nothing else: the envelope's attributes never enter a plan.
SignalRecordView.title: SignalRecordView

SourceChange.description: No fields: the address names the source and the change.
SourceChange.title: SourceChange

StartEntraConnect.description:
A new Microsoft Entra connection's name, or the consented connection whose consent to
update; never both.
StartEntraConnect.title: StartEntraConnect

StepUpResult.description: The session's new CSRF token; the session cookie itself changed in the same answer.
StepUpResult.title: StepUpResult

credential_id.description: The token's backing credential: every audit event the token caused names it as `actor_credential_id`, so this maps an event to the token's name.
credential_id.title: Credential Id

WeeklySummaryChange.description: Turn one's own summary on or off. No principal travels: the session is the person.
WeeklySummaryChange.title: WeeklySummaryChange

WeeklySummarySettings.description:
The person's own weekly summary (#678): whether the deployment sends it, whether it is
on, and the address it goes to, which is the person's own and null where none resolves.
WeeklySummarySettings.title: WeeklySummarySettings

info.description:
## Authentication

The console API is the console's own interface, and it accepts two kinds of caller.

- **A signed-in person**, in a browser: the session cookie, with the `X-CSRF-Token` header on every `POST`. This is how the console calls it.
- **A personal access token**, from a script or a tool such as a coding agent: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. An administrator creates their own token under **My account → Personal access tokens**; if they have enrolled a second factor, it must have been verified in the last thirty minutes, and an administrator with none enrolled is not asked for one. The token is shown once. It carries the administrator's authority, and every audit event it causes names the administrator and the token.

### What a token cannot do

A token acts as its owner, except where an audit log could only report afterwards what these refusals exist to prevent. Each answers 403 `TOKEN_NOT_ALLOWED`:

- **Decisions and settlement.** It cannot decide an approval, or settle or correct an execution's outcome.
- **Loosening enforcement.** It cannot activate a policy, switch the workspace to observe-only, lift an emergency stop, reactivate an agent, unarchive a space, or install the sample targets.
- **People, access and sign-in.** It cannot change people, access, approval rules, approvers, a space's member roster, invitations or account requests; change a workspace's sign-in; issue a person their own credential; or revoke a credential from the Credentials list, which can be a person's own sign-in credential.
- **The owner's own account and tokens.** It cannot read or switch the browser session, change its owner's password, sessions, profile, preferences or product-usage setting, or manage tokens.
- **Monitoring credentials and findings.** It cannot connect, re-key or revoke a monitoring connection, mint, rotate or revoke a reporting source, or acknowledge several findings at once.

Each operation below says whether a token may call it; the two whose rule depends on the request body say what it may not do. A token has its own rate limit of 300 requests per 60 seconds, and a request carrying a session cookie and a token together is refused.

A token's request may name a space with the `X-ExecBound-Space` header; without it, a token sees every space its owner can, and a write that needs one space answers 422 `SPACE_REQUIRED` in a workspace with several. A workspace that requires sign-in through an identity provider accepts no tokens (`DIRECTORY_REQUIRED`). An unknown, expired or revoked token answers 401 `SESSION_REQUIRED` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.

Agents do not call this API: they call the [agent API](/api/agent) with an API key.
info.title: ExecBound console API

schema.description:
A new draft: pasted JSON, a copy of the active bundle, or a rules file.

A copy is the paste: the active content is dumped, given a new identity and read back
through the page's own `parse_document`, so one path creates every draft and a copy
carries the ruleset a bundle written as rules holds. A rules file is the `Ruleset`
